user.title: Set up Hearth
user.description: Your household's Hearth TVs, phones and tablets pair with Home Assistant from their own settings (on a TV: Settings > Home Assistant > Pair with Home Assistant). Each one that asks shows up here to confirm.

confirm.title: Pair {name}?
confirm.description:
Check that {name} shows this code:

**{code}**

Pair it only if the codes match. A device you don't recognize, or a code that doesn't match, may be someone else's: close this instead.

data_description.person: For a phone or tablet: the person it belongs to. Its screen time counts for them.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Hearth is already set up. TVs and phones pair from their own settings.
abort.expired: This request has ended. Ask again from the TV or phone.

menu_options.enforce: Enforce limits (Family Link, Family Safety, Nintendo)
menu_options.group_apps: Add apps to Video or Games

people.title: Who's who on the TVs
people.description: Each Google TV profile the household's TVs have reported, and the person it is. A profile is listed by its name, once for all the TVs that have it; one from a TV with an older Hearth is listed for that TV only. Leave a guest or shared profile empty: its time counts for nobody. Old mappings by number (user:10) aren't listed: saving drops them. A profile not listed yet can be added below by its name ref (name:sam) or one TV's key (<device id>/user:11).

data.profile_id: Another profile's ref or TV key

add_group.title: Add a group
add_group.description: A group's apps count together against one budget, on every device. For example YouTube: YouTube and HearthTube.

group_apps.title: Add apps to Video or Games
group_apps.description: Apps Android marks as video or games are in these already. Add the ones it misses.

not_screen_time.title: Not screen time
not_screen_time.description: Groups whose time doesn't count toward All screen time (music, say). Their apps aren't held when All screen time runs out; a budget of their own still applies.

parent_pin.title: Parent PINs
parent_pin.description: Each adult's own parent PIN (set now: {people}). Any of them unlocks a parent's settings. Paired TVs use these in place of their own Parent PIN, and phones check them here; a phone never gets a PIN. They're kept as hashes. After 5 wrong tries a device waits, longer each time.

push.title: Push to phones
push.description: An ntfy server (ntfy.sh, or your own) through which Home Assistant tells a paired phone that something changed, so it fetches its state at once instead of at its next check. Each phone listens on its own random topic; the ping only says "changed", never a name or a number. Leave it empty for no pings.

tile_exchange.title: Tile exchange sharing
tile_exchange.description: People whose phone may share with the launcher's tile exchange: the layout of notifications from apps that have no tile yet, with every word and number blanked out (never chat, health or payment apps). Off for everyone not chosen here.

remove_group.title: Remove a group
remove_group.description: Its budgets and bonuses go with it.

add_source.title: Add a screen time source
add_source.description: Another integration's sensor: time today (Family Link's Daily Screen Time, Family Safety's Screen Time, Nintendo's Used screen time), or, with Live on, what's being played now (Xbox's Now playing, a Switch presence Game sensor), which Hearth times itself. If it's the same device as a Hearth device or another source, say so: its minutes are then counted once.

data.name: Name
data.live: Live: it says what's being played now

data_description.group: For time it can't put on an app: Games for a Switch or Xbox. A Nintendo Switch Parental Controls sensor is Games when left empty.

add_title.title: Add a title
add_title.description: One game or app by every name it has: the Android package, its name on Xbox and Switch, the PC app. Its time is counted together, and people on it at the same time are playing together.

locks.title: Locks
locks.description: Sensors that are on while this person may not watch, such as Family Link's bedtime and school time ones. While any is on, the person's Hearth devices hold their apps. Choosing a person again replaces their locks; none clears them.

new_apps.title: Watch for new apps
new_apps.description: Apps the kids start using on Hearth's devices are noticed by themselves. Add sensors that list a kid's allowed apps (Family Link's Apps without limits and Apps with time limits) to notice an app as soon as it's allowed. Requests for more time, offers and chores go to every adult's Home Assistant companion app, and to the phone chosen here, if any.

data.ask_off: Adults whose own phones don't get requests
data.ask_deep_link: Adults whose Android phones open hearth://ask/<id> (their own app) instead of Hearth's page

sort_apps.title: Sort new apps
sort_apps.description: The group each new app counts in. Other: only All screen time. Leave one empty to sort it later.

school_days.title: School days
school_days.description: Which budget applies today: the school-day one or the other-day one. Give any mix of these; the first that answers decides: the dates below, then the entity, then the calendar, then Monday to Friday within the school year.

data.entity: An entity that says what today is
data.school_states: Its states that mean a school day
data.keywords: Only events whose title has one of these words
data.year_start: First day of the school year
data.year_end: Last day of the school year
data.half_states: The entity's states that mean a half day
data.half_keywords: Calendar events that mean a half day

data_description.entity: A helper an automation keeps, the Workday integration's sensor, an input_boolean. Unavailable passes the question on.
data_description.school_states: Separated by commas. Leave empty for on, school, true, yes.
data_description.keywords: Separated by commas, for a calendar of days off: closed, break, holiday. Empty: any event.
data_description.days_off: Dates (2026-11-26) or ranges (2026-12-24..2027-01-01), separated by commas or new lines.
data_description.extra_school_days: Same, for days that are school days although they'd be off.
data_description.half_days: School days that end early, as dates or ranges. Schedule says what a half day does.
data_description.half_states: Separated by commas. Leave empty for half, half_day.
data_description.half_keywords: Words in an event's title (early dismissal, half day), separated by commas.

enforce.title: Enforce
enforce.description: When one of this person's groups is out of time, their Hearth TVs and phones stop its apps. Here, other parental controls can hold them too, until the group has time again (more time, a new day). Family Link pauses the group's Android apps (they stay installed; Google TV ignores this, Hearth holds the TV); for All screen time it locks the person's devices instead, and apps with unlimited time still work. Family Safety locks the platforms below while one of its groups below is out of time, until midnight. Nintendo suspends the Switch's game while one of its groups below is out of time (Max screentime today set to 0, with Suspend software on), and puts its limit and Suspend software back after. Choosing a person again replaces theirs; leaving them all empty stops it, and what was held is let go.

data.family_link: Family Link: any of the person's Family Link entities
data.family_safety: Family Safety: the person's account sensor
data.groups: Family Safety: lock while one of these groups is out of time
data.nintendo: Nintendo: the person's Switch (its Max screentime today)
data.nintendo_groups: Nintendo: suspend while one of these groups is out of time
data.nintendo_playing: A shared Switch: held only while this person is the one playing (their playing sensor)
data.school_time_apps: Family Link: during School time, pause these apps

data_description.school_time_apps: Paused while the person's Family Link School time is on (any of their devices), and resumed when it ends. Google Messages by default: it stays installed and keeps incoming texts. Empty: nothing.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.description: What each kind of day does to the kids' Family Link (the day type comes from School days). On a day off, School time can be switched off for the day; Hearth puts it back at the start of the next school day, inside each kid's own window. On a half day, School time can end some hours early. Both can give extra time: as Family Link's daily limit for today only (the weekday's limit plus the extra), as Family Safety's daily limits for today only (Windows, Xbox; off unless chosen), and/or as Hearth bonus minutes on a group. At the watchdog time on a school day, the adults are told if anyone's School time is still off.

data.half_day_hours_early: Half day: School time ends this many hours early
data.bonus_family_link: Extra minutes as Family Link's daily limit today
data.bonus_family_safety: Extra minutes as Family Safety's daily limits today (Windows, Xbox)
data.bonus_group: Extra minutes also as a Hearth bonus on this group
data.people: Who (empty: everyone with Family Link or Family Safety in Enforce)
data.notify: Tell this phone (empty: the one that answers requests for more time)

site_list.title: Website block list
site_list.description: Every day at this time, each person's Family Link blocked sites are brought in step with a published list (familylink.sync_site_list): new domains are added, and only what the list itself added before is taken out. A failure for one person is logged and the others go on.

data.people: Who (empty: everyone with Family Link or Family Safety in Enforce)

chores.title: Chores earn time
chores.description: Each chore checked off on the person's to-do list adds minutes to a group today, then goes from the list. A chore can say its own worth: "Dishes +30". Choosing a person again replaces theirs; no list stops it.

offer_more.title: Offer more time
offer_more.description: When one of these groups of the person's runs out, the adults are asked whether to give some more (the phone that answers requests for more time, and Hearth's page). Nothing is asked of the kid. Choosing a person again replaces theirs; no groups stops it.

data.groups: When one of these runs out

places.title: Places
places.description: Places are Home Assistant zones: Hearth keeps no coordinates and shows only a place's name. Home is always zone.home. Give a kid their school's zone (and, if Hearth doesn't find it, their Family Link location tracker): choosing a kid again replaces theirs. Add a favorite place by its zone and the name to show, or remove favorites. A router's or Wi-Fi tracker is never used. Favorites now: {favorites}.

data.tracker: Their Family Link location tracker (if not found)
data.favorite_zone: Add a favorite place: its zone

error.already_added: That sensor is a source already.
error.bad_profile_id: Give a ref like name:sam (or a TV's key, <device id>/user:11), and its person.
error.not_adult: Only an adult has a parent PIN: mark them as an adult on Hearth's page (Family) first.
error.bad_server: Give the server's address, like https://ntfy.example.com (no user name, password or query).
error.not_https: The address must start with https://
error.too_many_favorites: That's as many favorite places as Hearth keeps (20).

abort.no_profiles: No TV has reported its profiles yet. Pair a TV and let it post its status first.
abort.no_groups: There are no groups of your own to remove.

pause.name: Pause
pause.description: Holds the people's Hearth devices (dinner time, say) for some minutes, until a time, or until they arrive at or leave a place; they stop and show the reason. Everyone in the household when no one is chosen.

until.name: Until
until.description: Or until this time (tomorrow's, if it has passed today).

reason.name: Reason
reason.description: What the devices show, such as Dinner.

ends_on.name: Ends on
ends_on.description: Or ends sooner, for each person, when they arrive at a place or leave one: {"arrive": "home"}, {"leave": "school"} or a favorite place's key. The time (the end of the day when none is given) stays the cap; an unknown or stale place never ends it.

app.name: App
app.description: Pause only this app (its package name), not all screen time.

group.name: Group
group.description: Pause only this group's apps (its id or name, such as youtube), not all screen time.

pause_end.name: End the pause
pause_end.description: Lets the people go again (everyone paused when no one is chosen).

app.name: App
app.description: End only the pause of this app. With no app or group, only the family pause ends.

group.name: Group
group.description: End only the pause of this group.

add_bonus.name: Add a bonus
add_bonus.description: Adds minutes to a person's budget for today (a negative number takes them away).

group.name: Group
group.description: The group's id: all, video, games, or one of your own.

device.name: Device
device.description: Only on this device of theirs, today (a target id from the household summary: hearth:<id>, fl:<id>, fs:xbox, fs:windows, nintendo:<entity>): it may go past their shared time there. Only All screen time on a Family Link device, a Family Safety platform or a Switch.

set_budget.name: Set a budget
set_budget.description: Sets a person's daily budget for a group, on school days, other days, or both. Leave minutes empty for no limit.

group.name: Group
group.description: The group's id: all, video, games, or one of your own.

days.name: Days
days.description: school_days, other_days, or both (weekday and weekend are older names for the first two).

get_watch_log.name: Get the videos started
get_watch_log.description: The YouTube videos a person started in HearthTube in a kids profile, newest first, and what a parent blocked for them.

person.name: Person
person.description: Whose videos (a person with a TV profile).

days.name: Days
days.description: Only the last this many days (leave empty for all that is kept, up to 2,000).

watch_digest.name: Watch digest
watch_digest.description: One document for the last days: per kid, the videos started, counts per channel and per day, what was blocked, and a short readable summary.

person.name: Person
person.description: Whose (leave empty for everyone with a TV profile).

days.name: Days
days.description: How many days back (7: a week).

block_video.name: Block a video on YouTube
block_video.description: Blocks a video in HearthTube for a person's kids profiles. The kid can't undo it; the TV gets it with its next status (within a few minutes).

person.name: Person
person.description: For whom (a person with a TV profile).

video.name: Video
video.description: A video id or a YouTube link.

label.name: Label
label.description: What to show for it (a title, a name). Optional.

unblock_video.name: Unblock a video on YouTube
unblock_video.description: Takes back a video blocked here.

video.name: Video
video.description: A video id or a YouTube link.

block_channel.name: Block a channel on YouTube
block_channel.description: Blocks a channel in HearthTube for a person's kids profiles. The kid can't undo it; the TV gets it with its next status (within a few minutes).

person.name: Person
person.description: For whom (a person with a TV profile).

channel.name: Channel
channel.description: A channel id (UC...) or a youtube.com/channel/ link; a handle (@name) won't do.

label.name: Label
label.description: What to show for it (a title, a name). Optional.

unblock_channel.name: Unblock a channel on YouTube
unblock_channel.description: Takes back a channel blocked here.

channel.name: Channel
channel.description: A channel id (UC...) or a youtube.com/channel/ link; a handle (@name) won't do.

block_word.name: Block a word on YouTube
block_word.description: Blocks a word in HearthTube for a person's kids profiles. The kid can't undo it; the TV gets it with its next status (within a few minutes).

person.name: Person
person.description: For whom (a person with a TV profile).

word.name: Word
word.description: A word or words; videos whose title has it are hidden (titles only).

unblock_word.name: Unblock a word on YouTube
unblock_word.description: Takes back a word blocked here.

word.name: Word
word.description: A word or words; videos whose title has it are hidden (titles only).

play_on_tv.name: Play on a TV
play_on_tv.description: Starts a link, a YouTube video (in HearthTube) or an app on a Hearth TV. The TV takes it with its next status, within about 2 minutes while it's on, and plays it as if picked there: a kids profile's limits and blocks still apply. Answers the command's id; hearth_command_done says how it went.

device_id.name: TV
device_id.description: The Hearth TV (its device, or its Hearth device id).

what.name: What
what.description: A link (http or https), a YouTube video id or link, or an app's package name (com.example.app).

profile.name: Profile
profile.description: Optional: the TV profile to play it in (an id like user:10, or a person with one profile on the TV). The TV switches to it first, asking for its PIN as usual.

allow.name: Allow
allow.description: Lets people use an app or a group until a time: while it lasts, Hearth holds it nowhere for them (their TVs and phones, Family Link, the School-time pause). Bedtime, School time itself and a family pause still lock them. Returns its id.

app.name: App
app.description: One app, by its package name. Or a group.

group.name: Group
group.description: A Hearth group (youtube), or all for everything Hearth holds.

until.name: Until
until.description: A time (tomorrow's if it has passed), school_time_end (the end of their School time today) or end_of_day (the default).

ends_on.name: Ends on
ends_on.description: Or ends sooner, for each person, when they arrive at a place or leave one: {"arrive": "home"}, {"leave": "school"} or a favorite place's key. The time stays the cap; an unknown or stale place never ends it.

device.name: Device
device.description: Only on this device of theirs (a target id): the group is open there until the time. Only All screen time on a Family Link device, a Family Safety platform or a Switch.

allow_end.name: End an allow
allow_end.description: Ends an allow early: by its id, or the people's (of an app or a group, when given). A parent's grant (from the Family Link, Nintendo or Family Safety app) ends by its id too. What should hold then holds again.

id.name: Id
id.description: The id hearth.allow returned, or a parent grant's id.

device.name: Device
device.description: End the extra time given on this device (a target id): its bonus or allow there.

explain.name: Explain
explain.description: Why an app or a group is held for a person now, or isn't: allowed, until, blocked_by (budget, bedtime, school_time, pause, school_time_apps), and the allows that apply.

app.name: App
app.description: An app, by its package name. Or a group.

school_time_off.name: School time off
school_time_off.description: Switches the people's Family Link School time off on a date (today by default), from a time if given. Hearth puts it back at the start of their next school day, inside each one's own window, and pins today's hours.

people.name: People
people.description: Who (each needs Family Link in Configure > Enforce).

from.name: From
from.description: From this time; the whole day when empty.

ends_on.name: Ends on
ends_on.description: Today only: School time comes back sooner, for each person, when they arrive at a place or leave one: {"arrive": "school"}, {"leave": "home"} or a favorite place's key. An unknown or stale place never ends it.

school_time_off_cancel.name: Cancel School time off
school_time_off_cancel.description: One not started yet is dropped; one already off is put back from today (inside the window, as always).

answer_request.name: Answer a request for more time
answer_request.description: Answers a kid's request for more time (or an offer): more minutes today, or not now. The first answer wins; a later one is refused. Returns the request as its device sees it.

request_id.name: Request
request_id.description: The request's id (the household summary's approvals, or the hearth_more_time_requested event).

minutes.name: Minutes
minutes.description: Extra minutes today (1-600). Give this or Deny.

deny.name: Deny
deny.description: Not now (starts a short wait before the kid may ask again).

copy_sites.name: Copy websites between Family Link and Family Safety
copy_sites.description: Copies a kid's blocked (or allowed) websites from Family Link to Family Safety, the other way round, or both. Only adds: a site with a path isn't copied, a site a website list sync added is left to it, and a site blocked on one side and allowed on the other is left on both. Returns, per person, what was added and what was left.

people.name: People
people.description: Whose websites (everyone with both Family Link and Family Safety in Configure > Enforce when none).

from.name: From
from.description: Which side's sites are copied to the other: family_link, family_safety or both.

lists.name: Lists
lists.description: Which lists: blocked (the default), allowed or both.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: Only say what would be added, without adding anything.

tv_profile_keys.title: Pick the kids' TV profiles again
tv_profile_keys.description: Hearth used to map TV profiles by their number ({keys}), but each TV numbers its profiles itself: the same number is a different kid on each TV, so one kid could get another's limits. Those mappings are no longer used. Open Hearth's page (Devices, TV profiles) or Hearth's Configure menu and pick whose each profile is. Profiles are now listed by name, one choice for every TV. Removing or replacing the old entries clears this message.
